title: this / bind / call / apply
description: this is decided by how a function is CALLED. Four call patterns (method, standalone, new, explicit) + the arrow gotcha (lexical capture).

notes: this is bound at CALL time for normal functions; arrow functions capture this at DEFINITION time.
bind returns a new function; call/apply invoke immediately. apply takes args as an array.
Passing a method as a callback (setTimeout, map) detaches it — wrap in arrow or bind to preserve this.

questions.q: When is `this` resolved for a regular (non-arrow) function?
options: When the function is called — based on how it is called
call binds permanently, apply does not
apply takes args as an array; call takes them comma-separated
The result of calling the function
A new function with this (and optional args) locked in
The original function mutated in place

questions.q: Inside `obj.greet() { return (() => this.name)(); }`, the arrow’s `this` is:
options: obj — arrows inherit this from the enclosing scope
